audit:public-guest.area: public-guest: public and guest-facing pages (guest theme) and auth pages
audit:public-guest.summary: The guest theme itself is in good shape: every page wrapped in GuestShell (table-payment, table-manage, event-payment, manage-booking, waitlist-offer, private-feedback, email-capture, booking-portal, parking, invoice-portal, legacy-link, privacy, the three feedback pages) uses only anchor-*/guest-* colours, no staff tokens leak into them and no guest tokens leak into staff screens. The weakness is that the guest system has colour tokens but no type, tracking, spacing or control-height tokens, so the handoff's exact values are typed out as about 345 arbitrary values (text-[14px], leading-[1.6], tracking-[0.16em], gap-[18px]); roughly 320 of those are faithful to HANDOFF.md and around 20 have already drifted (heading line-heights, label tracking, two copies of the success card). The real visible inconsistencies are the pages that sit outside both systems: the live SMS "Are you still coming?" page (/g/[token]/confirm-booking) is plain grey Tailwind with an emerald button and no Anchor branding, the retired card-capture and sunday-preorder landings are raw grey or the old dark-green shell, and email-capture's submit is a green 10px-radius button while every other guest primary is a gold pill. On the staff side, the sign-in journey has four different looks (light .auth card for login, full-screen dark green for reset-password and reset, a frosted glass card for recover, and a slate and teal inline HTML page from /auth/confirm), and global-error is cool grey with blue buttons. From reading the code (not rendered), the reset-password "Check your email" state puts dark stone text straight onto the dark green background, which will be close to unreadable.

audit:public-guest.fix_notes: Suggested order, each independently shippable. (1) Move /g/[token]/confirm-booking onto GuestShell, GuestCard and GuestButton; this needs name/value props on GuestButton first. Do card-capture and sunday-preorder in the same pass and delete src/components/features/shared/GuestPageShell.tsx (only sunday-preorder imports it). (2) Replace the email-capture raw submit with GuestButton and remove the dead checkbox utilities there and in LegacyLinkClient. (3) Put /auth/reset-password, /auth/reset and /auth/recover on the same .auth shell as /auth/login, put the EmptyState inside the card, and restyle the /auth/confirm inline HTML with @theme hex values; set .auth__card radius to var(--radius-lg). (4) Restyle global-error with DS Button and Card and check whether it needs its own globals.css import (not verified by rendering). (5) Tokenise the guest system in @theme: type scale with paired line-heights, tracking, control heights, container width and soft/border tints; add GUEST_H2_CLASS, GUEST_LABEL_CLASS, a guestButtonClassName helper, GuestSuccessCard, GuestHelpLine and GuestIconBadge; this removes most of the ~345 arbitrary values and fixes the ~20 drifted ones mechanically. The (dev)/guest-preview harness (404 in production) is exempt but should be updated with any new primitives. No dead duplicate *Client.tsx files were found in this area: every file in scope is imported by its route. Open questions for the owner: should the recruitment booking page use the Anchor guest brand, should the invoice portal carry Anchor or Orange Jelly branding, and which green should the favicon use. No lint rule stops raw palette classes in guest files; a simple ESLint or test guard over src/app/g and src/components/features/guest would stop regressions.

audit:generated-documents.area: generated-documents: emails, PDFs, printable HTML and colour constants (src/lib, src/app/api, src/types, src/services, src/app/actions)
audit:generated-documents.summary: Emails, PDFs and printouts have no single source of truth for colour. The only shared pieces are the marketing email block library (a consistent Anchor guest palette, checked byte for byte by fixture tests), the finance-document chrome in src/lib/pdf/document-chrome.ts and the guest contact footer. Everything else hardcodes its own palette: about 1,235 hex literals across 98 source files (148 distinct values), and the staff primary #006A4E and the warm stone neutrals (#1c1917, #57534e, #ececea) are used zero times, so no email or PDF matches the app. Customers see black, near-black, Anchor green, gold, PayPal blue or bright green buttons depending on which email or page they get. Staff get rota emails with four different button colours and a printed rota whose colours do not match the screen, and status colours drift: "Couldn't Work" is blue in the hours PDF and red everywhere else, and invoice PDF badges are saturated fills with white text that fails contrast. The only token-like constants in this area are dead: THEME_COLORS in src/lib/constants.ts (which claims primary is blue), the unexported CHANNEL_COLOURS, and src/ds/tokens/index.ts, which exports nothing.

categories.description: Hex and rgba colour literals in inline email styles, Puppeteer PDF CSS, pdfkit calls and SVG charts. My count is about 1,235 hex in 98 non-test source files, plus 13 rgba. HTML entities such as ​ and ͏ are excluded, as are the 34 __fixtures__ HTML files (1,828 if you include them). This is close to the 1,252 in areas.json. Each template picks its own values instead of importing a shared palette.
categories.correct_approach: Hex is required here because CSS variables do not work in email clients or pdfkit, but every value should come from one module of literal hex values that mirrors globals.css (for example src/lib/brand/palette.ts with STAFF and GUEST objects), guarded by a parity test against the @theme block, in the same way the deposit rule is pinned by a parity test. Emails and PDFs then import named constants instead of typing hex.
categories.exempt_reason: Email clients and PDF renderers (pdfkit, Puppeteer print) need literal colour values; CSS custom properties from globals.css are not available. The drift between values is still a real problem even though literals are allowed.

Everything else, above all /settings/table-bookings (151 raw, 0 token) and the dish drawer on /menu-management and /menu-management/dishes (196 raw, 0 token), mixes warm-stone DS components with cool-gray hand-written markup, so staff see two slightly different greys, three input heights and three label styles on one screen. The same patterns recur across files: gray "mini cards" (18 copies), amber, blue and green callouts written by hand instead of Alert (about 17), hand-made status pills instead of Badge, icon buttons instead of IconButton, and raw tables instead of Table, so a handful of DS swaps would remove most of the raw colour. Some of the damage is functional as well as visual: coloured borders on the special-hours calendar never show because the class conflicts with its base colour, the GP target % suffix and the background-job status icons never render, and alerts on the table setup page cannot be closed. Two DS components that every page here depends on, Section (title in text-gray-900) and DataTable (header bg-gray-50, green-500 focus rings), emit raw gray themselves, so even the "compliant" pages show cool gray headings and tables.

tailwind-compile-check.summary: The compiler found only four dead Tailwind classes in live code: prose and prose-sm (the typography plugin is not installed), bg-surface-muted and border-guest-line (neither token exists). The larger problems come from three other sources. First, the theme changes what familiar names mean: rounded-md is 10px, rounded-lg is 14px, bare rounded is 4px (smaller than rounded-sm), rounded-2xl is 16px (smaller than rounded-xl), and shadow, shadow-md and shadow-xl are still stock black Tailwind shadows that ignore the slate-tinted tokens. Second, cn() is stock tailwind-merge with no token config. Colour tokens merge correctly, but custom radius, shadow, spacing and ease tokens do not, and one real bug follows from it: every DS Input, Select and Textarea in its error state shows the green focus halo instead of the red one. Third, unlayered rules in globals.css beat every utility regardless of specificity. They force 64 grids to one column on phones, and they override the padding on 83 raw text-sm buttons. Separately, 76 elements draw borders in the text colour because Tailwind v4 has no default grey border and globals.css adds no compatibility rule. No class name is built at runtime anywhere classes are applied.
tailwind-compile-check.method: All scripts are in scratchpad/tw. Because main-src has no node_modules, globals.css was copied byte for byte to scratchpad/tw/app, with a node_modules symlink beside it so that @import "tailwindcss" resolves. (1) extract.cjs parses every non-test .ts/.tsx file in main-src/src (1,678 files) with the TypeScript compiler API. It collects string literals and template pieces from className and *ClassName JSX attributes, from cn/clsx/cva/twMerge arguments, from class- or style-named variables and lookup maps, and from the returns of tone, variant or colour functions. It also keeps other strings where at least half of the tokens compile, and it skips comparison operands and non-class call arguments. Every token (45,435 occurrences, 33,330 unique) was tested with __unstable__loadDesignSystem(globals.css).candidatesToCss(), which gives the exact per-class CSS output of Tailwind 4.3.0. Selectors defined in globals.css were excluded, and the remaining no-CSS tokens were read by hand. (2) As an independent recall check, oxide-pass.cjs ran Tailwind's own oxide Scanner.getCandidatesWithPositions over the same files. It kept no-CSS candidates whose root is one of the 1,210 real utility roots and reviewed them by hand; everything it added was comments, data or HTML/CSS template strings. (3) resolve.cjs printed the CSS and theme values for the requested utilities. order.cjs and getClassOrder() gave Tailwind's output order, which decides the winner when two conflicting classes are both kept. (4) twm.cjs ran the stock tailwind-merge 3.5.0 bundle. merge-impact.cjs compared stock twMerge with an extendTailwindMerge that knows the custom tokens, across every statically resolvable cn() call and every DS component usage with a static className. conflicts.cjs checked single class strings for internal conflicts (1 found, harmless). cascade.cjs checked, per JSX element, which elements the unlayered globals.css selectors hit and which borders have no colour. A compiled sample confirmed that those selectors sit outside @layer utilities. Template fragments (8,313) were screened for runtime-built classes. None of this was checked in a browser.

audit:customers-events-comms.summary: The area is split roughly in two. The newer screens (private bookings list, events list and detail, the /messages inbox, marketing, short links, feedback inbox) are close to fully tokenised. The older screens (private booking detail, its items/messages/SMS queue/settings pages, the booking calendar, customer detail and insights, bulk messages, the event category form and the shared modals) use no tokens at all, only raw cool gray-* and blue-* classes. About 1,171 raw palette classes (858 of them gray) sit against about 700 token classes. Staff will notice several things: two neutral families on one screen (DS cards in warm stone around gray-500/gray-900 text); customer links that are green in one table and blue in another; blue selected states and blue chat bubbles where the rest of the app uses brand green; the same status ('completed', 'scheduled', 'queued', 'cancelled', 'fully paid') in different colours on different pages. A few genuine rendering faults come from Tailwind v4 defaults: borders with no colour draw a black line, the emergency-contact inputs have no visible border, and the 'Send Reminder' button shows dark text on orange.

token-system-inventory.summary:
Yes, the app has design tokens: 103 of them in the @theme block of src/app/globals.css (lines 8 to 172). That is 45 staff colours, 23 guest colours, 5 fonts, 12 spacing, 1 breakpoint, 8 radius, 8 shadow and 1 easing. Newer code and most of src/ds use them heavily: text-text-muted appears 1,085 times, border-border 470, text-text 355, text-text-strong 295, bg-primary and related 188. The system itself has traps that cause much of the inconsistency.

1. The radius tokens override Tailwind's own names. rounded-sm is 6px, rounded-md 10px, rounded-lg 14px and rounded-xl 20px, but rounded-2xl is still Tailwind's 16px, so 2xl is smaller than xl. Bare rounded is still 4px, which is off the scale. I confirmed this by compiling globals.css with the repo's Tailwind 4.3.0. There are 451 rounded-md, 372 rounded-lg and 225 bare rounded uses.
2. Only xs, sm, lg and ring shadows are custom. Bare shadow (50 uses), shadow-md (8) and shadow-xl (20) still give Tailwind's pure-black defaults, and the custom shadow-default is never used.
3. The tokens are a warm stone grey, but the app has 3,205 raw gray-* classes, which are Tailwind v4's cool, blue-tinted grey. The most common raw class, text-gray-500 (659 uses), has no matching token: text-muted is much darker, and text-subtle fails WCAG AA at 2.5:1.
4. --color-sidebar is being used as the dark green for FOH, voucher and auth buttons and focus rings in about 20 files. It also duplicates --color-sidebar-bg.
5. Staff screens show at least five greens: primary #006A4E, sidebar #064e3b, SectionNav's hardcoded #005131 (used by 21 files), success #16a34a and 343 raw green-* classes.
6. Toast.tsx points to tokens that do not exist (--color-success-surface and similar), so it always falls back to hex. About 72 files skip it and call react-hot-toast directly.
7. The legacy shadcn HSL :root block is still used by two FOH files. Its --primary is a slightly different green.
8. src/ds/tokens/index.ts exports nothing (`export {}`), so the JavaScript token accessors are dead code.
9. --spacing-row-h is 10px and is actually used as table cell padding. It was planned as a 29px row height.
10. There are no tokens for the sizes the app really uses: 13px, 11px and 10px text make up 298 of about 428 arbitrary text-[..] values. There is also nothing for line-height, z-index, overlays, focus ring colour, disabled state, status borders, chart or category colours, the table header, or on-dark surfaces.
11. Some tokens fail contrast: text-subtle is 2.52:1 on white, border-focus 1.92:1, and success, warning and info are below 4.5:1 when used as text.
12. The guidance is stale or missing. docs/standards/UI_UX.md, which docs/README.md calls "START HERE", describes components that no longer exist and a tailwind.config file. Nothing enforces token use.

Where counts come from my own regex pass, they exclude tests and src/ds/tokens/index.ts, and are close to the baseline you gave. Everything was read from the origin/main snapshot at 9ebaaff5. Nothing in the repo was changed.

js_accessor_issues: src/ds/tokens/index.ts:95 ends with `export {}`. getToken, colors, spacing, shadows, radii and easing are all private to the module. The barrel re-export at src/ds/index.ts:13 (`export * from './tokens'`) therefore exports nothing, and no file imports @/ds/tokens. The exports were removed by the knip prune in commit dc0ca8a09. The original plan (.planning/phases/01-design-system-app-shell/01-01-PLAN.md:32) required colors, spacing and shadows to be exported.

colors is incomplete. It has sidebarBg but not sidebar, which is the name with 106 uses. It lacks sidebarFgMuted, sidebarActiveBg, sidebarHoverBg and sidebarBorder, and all 23 anchor-* and guest-* colours.

spacing lacks logoRow and pageShellPadY. There are no entries for fonts (sans, mono, anchor-*), the shell breakpoint, or guest radius and shadow tokens. Nothing lists a token that does not exist, and no value is stale, because every entry is a var() string.

The accessors return var(--x) strings, not actual colours, so they cannot be used for canvas drawing. src/components/charts/BarChart.tsx, the case the file says it is for, hardcodes #3B82F6, #E5E7EB, #6B7280 and #374151 instead (lines 26, 117, 140, 235).

getToken() reads getComputedStyle on the root element. Tailwind v4 only writes a theme variable to :root if something references it: compiling globals.css with no candidates emitted only 27 variables. So getToken would return an empty string for any token not referenced elsewhere. Today the var() strings in this dead file happen to make Tailwind emit every token, which is the file's only live effect.
Recommendation: either delete the file or export typed accessors that include resolved values and are used by Chart.tsx, BarChart.tsx and the design-system page, which would then stop hardcoding hex.

audit:ds-foundation.summary: The core primitives (Button, Badge, Alert, Input, Select, Textarea, Field, Card, Modal, Drawer, Tabs, Table, Checkbox, Radio, Switch, Stat) use the semantic colour tokens correctly, and Badge and Alert use exactly the same success/warning/danger/info tokens. But several heavily used composites were never moved onto tokens. PageLayout (92 files), DataTable (12), Pagination (8), Section (47) and the compat TabNav, RadioGroup and Accordion still use Tailwind's cool gray and bright green-500/600. SectionNav hardcodes the guest Anchor gold and green as hex. So staff see two page chromes (a warm stone background versus a gray-100 page with a white header band), three different tab styles, two table header styles and at least six focus-ring styles, and /invoices and /short-links/insights show two of the tab styles stacked on one screen. Beyond colour: the Inter font token is not linked to the next/font variable, the DS Toast reads CSS variables that do not exist (so its info toast is blue while Alert and Badge info are sky), 70 files bypass the DS toast altogether, the JS token accessors export nothing, and the style guide page covers under half the tokens and none of the components that cause the inconsistency. Counts come from a regex scan plus a check against the real Tailwind v4 compiler on the origin/main snapshot, so treat them as estimates.

audit:ds-foundation.fix_notes: This is a small number of files with a wide reach. About 15 DS files cause most of the visible inconsistency, and every screen inherits from them, so fixing them restyles 150+ screens without touching the screens themselves. Suggested order. (1) Token wiring, no visual decisions needed: point --font-sans and --font-mono at the next/font variables; point Toast at the real status tokens and give the global Toaster DS toastOptions so the 70 direct react-hot-toast callers match; re-export or delete ds/tokens/index.ts and move Chart onto it. (2) Retokenise the legacy composites with the high-confidence mappings above: PageLayout (background, header band, title, breadcrumbs, loader), DataTable (rebuild on Table), Pagination (merge with TablePagination on Button/Select/Input), Section, Accordion, compat TabNav, RadioGroup and SortableHeader, AuthenticatedLayout loaders and error.tsx. (3) Add the missing tokens the DS already needs: text-ui 13px, text-2xs, shadow-ring-danger, an overlay scrim, an AA-safe avatar palette, and staff nav tokens if the gold/green SectionNav look is kept. Then replace arbitrary values with the generated utilities (h-btn-h, p-pad-card, py-row-h, rounded-default, rounded-pill, max-shell:). (4) Unify the form label style, the focus ring (shadow-ring everywhere) and button radii. (5) Rebuild the style guide so it reads token values from CSS and renders PageLayout, DataTable, Tabs, SectionNav, Modal, Drawer and Toast live. Decisions the owner needs to make: whether SectionNav keeps the Anchor gold/green or moves to primary; one page chrome (PageLayout band or PageHeader on stone); one table header style; one label style. Risk: PageLayout and DataTable changes land on about 100 screens at once, so each needs a visual pass at desktop and 375px, especially the PageLayout negative-margin fix. Afterwards add a guard (a Vitest scan or ESLint rule) that fails on raw palette classes and hex inside src/ds, since nothing enforces tokens today. Dead files to remove separately: NetworkStatus.tsx, and BackButton, FormSubmitButton and DescriptionList if they stay unused.

audit:money.summary: This area is split in two. Cashing up, OJ projects, the dashboard and most of receipts are close to fully tokenised (0 raw palette classes in cashing-up, oj-projects and dashboard; receipts about 3% raw). The older invoice and quote screens, expenses, mileage destinations and the trip form are 77 to 95% raw Tailwind cool gray, red, green and blue. The invoice and quote list pages are clean, but their detail, new, edit, recurring, vendor and catalog pages are not, so staff see warm stone neutrals on one click and cool gray the next. The most visible faults: about 27 bare `border` or `border-t` classes draw near-black lines, because Tailwind v4 defaults border colour to currentColor. The expenses form has a blue primary button and blue focus rings, and turns dark grey on a device set to dark mode. Two receipts grid layouts are broken by comma syntax. The same invoice status or "outstanding" amount is coloured differently on /invoices, the invoice detail page and /oj-projects/clients. Charts use at least five different greens and three reds for the same meanings, and there are no chart tokens.

audit:foh-table-bookings.summary: Token compliance in this area is poor. Across 67 files there are about 1,099 raw Tailwind palette classes against about 206 token classes (roughly 16% token share). Only parking, MessageGuestsModal and the event check-in kiosk are built mostly from tokens. The FOH swimlane, the FOH modals, BOH and the whole vouchers FOH screen are hand-built from cool gray-*, red/amber/green and bg-sidebar, often with no @/ds components at all (15 of the 44 UI files import nothing from @/ds). The same booking status gets different colours and badge shapes on different screens, and the same voucher gets a different colour and label on FOH ("Active", green) than on the ledger ("Issued", blue). Controls in FOH modals and the clock widget stay under 44px on the bar iPad in landscape, because the touch-target rule only reaches content inside the FOH wrapper and every Headless UI modal is portalled outside it. Much of the booking-status colour is centralised in src/lib/table-bookings/ui.ts, which makes that part cheap to fix, but its badge map and its timeline-block map disagree with each other and with the DS Badge tones.

visual_inconsistencies.issue: Primary confirm buttons use four different greens and one page uses blue. On FOH, 'Create booking' and 'Change time' are bg-sidebar (#064e3b); the FOH 'Clock In' modal is bg-green-600 (#16a34a); the timeclock PIN confirm is bg-green-700 (#15803d); DS Button primary on booking detail, BOH and the clock-out ConfirmDialog is #006A4E. The manager-kiosk hover goes from #064e3b to green-700, a lighter and different hue. Reports shows its selected window and chart bars in blue.

The same booking status shows in different colours depending on where you look. In ui.ts the badge map and the swimlane block map disagree (left: gray badge, sky block; completed: gray badge, blue block; pending payment: yellow badge, amber block). The 'Booked' (green-100) and 'Seated' (emerald-100) badges are nearly the same colour. The customer page uses its own three-colour regex, so a cancelled booking is red there but gray on FOH and BOH, and completed is green there but gray or blue here.

The same voucher shows a different colour and label on the FOH screen and on the management pages. FOH: issued is green 'Active', redeemed is slate 'Used', expired is red. Ledger and detail (DS Badge): issued is blue 'Issued', redeemed is green 'Redeemed', expired is amber.

FOH touch targets on the bar iPad in landscape. The manager-kiosk variant shrinks controls to 9 to 11px text with py-1. Swimlane block text is 9 to 10px. The 44px coarse-pointer rule does not reach portalled modals (create booking, booking detail no-show and cancel confirms, change time, clock-in) or the clock widget pills in the page header, so those stay at about 26 to 36px.

Status and deposit badge shapes differ for the same data. Booking detail uses 4px square uppercase badges; the FOH detail modal and outside list use 10px rounded rectangles; BOH uses 11px pills; deposit badges are pills on FOH and BOH but 4px on booking detail. DS Badge pills sit alongside them in the same modal.

Selected-chip styles differ for the same 'Won at' and filter choice. Vouchers FOH uses a filled dark-green pill; Hand-out mode and the ledger use an outlined green-600 chip on green-50; reports uses blue; FOH and BOH view toggles use a white-on-gray segment.

Two neutral families on one screen. Cool gray-* cards and text sit next to warm stone token components: the gray SectionCard on booking detail holds the token-styled RefundHistoryTable; the swimlane mixes token BookingBadges with gray lanes; voucher overview DS Cards (warm border) carry gray-500/gray-900 text.
Focus rings differ from control to control. There are at least 8 ring colours in the area, none matching the DS shadow-ring, and 15 raw FOH fields show the browser default outline instead.

Card and control radius varies. Cards are 14px (rounded-lg), 20px (rounded-xl on the FOH kiosk and vouchers FOH) or 8px (event kiosk). Buttons are 10px raw, 8px DS or 14px on vouchers FOH. Bare `rounded` gives 4px, which is off the app scale.

The drag-to-move confirmation looks unlike every other FOH modal. It uses legacy shadcn HSL variables, so it has cool slate text (#020817 and #64748b), 4px buttons and pinkish off-white text on the confirm button (--primary-foreground is 355.7 100% 97.3%).

Native checkboxes on FOH create booking and the party-size edit render in the browser default colour (blue on iPad), not primary green. Their text-sidebar and text-green-600 classes do nothing without a forms plugin.

The timeclock kiosk mixes families. A cool gray-900 layout background sits behind the brand-700 .kiosk panel, toasts are hex gray-800, and the PIN modal is white with gray text and a green-700 button. The event check-in kiosk does the same job with brand tokens and DS components. The .kiosk negative margins (meant for the app shell) also apply on this shell-less route at iPad-landscape widths, which may leave a gray band or a slight horizontal overflow (not verified in a browser).

audit:people-ops.area: people-ops: employees, rota, staff portal, onboarding, roles, users, profile, checklists, maintenance, recruitment
audit:people-ops.summary: This area is split in two. The newer screens (rota, recruitment, maintenance, profile, users, most of checklists) use the tokens: about 97% token share in rota and 100% in recruitment and maintenance. The older screens hardly use them at all: the staff portal has 0 token classes across 10 files, the components/features/employees tabs are about 1% tokens (roughly 400 raw classes), and 6 of the 8 onboarding steps, plus the /roles forms, use raw Tailwind classes. Staff will see two different greens on primary buttons (brand #006A4E against Tailwind green-600 #16a34a) and cool gray text sitting next to the warm stone DS surfaces. The same status also changes colour from screen to screen: Couldn't Work is red on /rota but blue on /rota/hours, and kitchen is amber on the rota grid but orange on templates and in the portal. There are 15 bespoke modals with three different backdrop tints. On /employees/[id], /roles/new and /roles/[id]/edit, several form fields probably render with no border, because they rely on the missing @tailwindcss/forms plugin. I worked that out from the CSS rules and have not checked it in a browser.

verify:canonical-mapping.notes:
Method: a scripted count over main-src/src (1,680 .ts/.tsx files, tests excluded) found 5,053 raw palette class uses including white and black (about 4,600 without them), in line with the baseline. Scripts and output are in scratchpad/recon (count.mjs, bare.mjs, pal.mjs, counts.json, bare.txt). The raw hex figures are Tailwind 4.3.0 oklch values from node_modules/tailwindcss/theme.css, converted to sRGB. Visual-change bands use OKLab distance: none below 0.02, subtle 0.02 to 0.06, noticeable above 0.06. Tailwind output was checked by compiling candidates against the snapshot's globals.css. codemod_safe=true means one regex swap is correct in nearly every context. false means someone has to judge each site or swap in a component.

Findings the areas missed or got wrong:
1. src/ds/tokens/index.ts:95 is `export {};`, so getToken, colors and radii cannot be imported. Every JS or canvas token proposal needs that export restored first.
2. Borders with no colour draw in currentColor under Tailwind v4 (preflight sets border: 0 solid and globals.css has no override). I confirmed 9 dark outlines on invoice, quote and private-booking pages (listed in the mappings).
3. There are 62 dark: classes in the expenses form and file viewer. No @custom-variant exists, so they switch on with the OS setting: a manager using dark mode sees a dark grey form inside a light app.
4. max-[820px]: compiles to width < 820px, but the CSS mobile layer is max-width: 820px, so the two disagree at exactly 820px. max-shell: fixes this.
5. The 'exact match' claims for red-600, green-600, amber-600 and gray-900 rest on Tailwind v3 hex. In v4 the difference is small but real.
6. The four legacy text-muted hits are documentation strings, not live classes.
7. src/lib/constants.ts:34 THEME_COLORS is unexported, unused and stale (primary '#2563eb').
8. The base status tokens fail AA as small text on white: text-success 3.30:1, text-warning 3.19:1, text-info 4.10:1. Small status text should use the -fg tokens.
9. bg-sidebar (#064e3b) is the same hex as primary-hover.

Recommended codemod order: (a) the value-equal swaps marked none or subtle, which touch roughly 2,600 uses (gray-200/300/50/100, bg-white, gray-600/800/900, red-600, -50 fills, radius and arbitrary-var cleanups, text-[12/14/16px], min-h). (b) text-gray-500 and text-gray-700, which darken secondary and label text across the app and should ship as one owner-approved release. (c) Manual, context-dependent work: focus rings, selected states, links to primary, status borders, and buttons to DS Button. Rows marked 'estimate' are estimates. No lint rule enforces tokens today, so without a guard (for example an ESLint no-restricted-syntax rule or a test that fails on new raw palette classes) the drift will come back.

Open decisions for the owner, to be raised in chat by the main agent: links turning from blue to brand green; FOH buttons moving from sidebar green to primary; the black staff-portal CTAs; the SectionNav Anchor green and gold; the table-booking status badge tones; and the minimum font size (raising 9px and below to 10px).
